trickyParts: Dispatch has no create-only upload: an upload of a known name replaces its text (artifacts.go:445-516). The rule 'never uploaded twice to effect' rests on Dispatch's Idempotency-Key, agreed with the architect: the create is a fixed header-only body for the session under the key askgate-doc.<sha256(project, name)>, and every record, the first included, is a doc-edit insert at the end under askgate-rec.<sha256(session, record id)>. A repeat create is replayed, 409 KEY_IN_FLIGHT (the client retries), 409 KEY_COMMITTED or 422 KEY_REUSED; the last two go to the read by name and the append, never a second upload.

Fact 1, the key's scope: Dispatch scopes a key to its login (requestKeyLogin, request_keys.go:465-476). Every Legion pod writes under the shared agent token (login `agent-token`; `dispatch whoami`: 'runs under the shared token: no owner'), and a session's document carries its session id, so every process writing it shares one scope. Residual: a session whose processes write under two different logins while a create is in flight, which one deployment does not produce.

Fact 2, the key's retention: IdempotencyKeyTTL is 24 h (contracts/generated.go:268) and a keyed handler's run is bounded by keyedHandlerLimit, 10 min (request_keys.go:103), so a create's late commit always lands while its key is remembered; past 24 h a create runs only on a 404, since the read by name comes first.
